_comment: Useful phrases (Redemittel) by speech act: agreeing, disagreeing, doubting, comforting … Each set is a flashcard deck (/vocabulary/phrases/<id>) and a row under the phrases on /pronunciation. The key `de` holds the French phrase that is practised (the key name is history, see docs/content-plan.md §1.4); `en` is the English meaning, with a short usage note where it helps. Register: phrases use tu with friends and vous with strangers, officials and colleagues you don't know well; the note says which, and gives the other form where it matters. Every phrase has `variety`, and `frCA` where Québec usage differs. Phrase order matters: the beginner path refers to phrases as redemittel:<set>#<index>, so a phrase keeps its slot (same speech act, same position). Translations live in src/data/redemittel-i18n/<lang>.json, keyed by the French phrase: machine drafts until a native speaker has read them (reviewed: false). Audio: scripts/generate-satz-audio.mjs → public/audio/redemittel/<slug>.mp3 (none yet for the French phrases).

phrases.en: You're right. (To someone you call vous: Vous avez raison.)

phrases.de: Je suis tout à fait d'accord.
phrases.en: I completely agree.
Exactly!
I agree with you. (With vous: avec vous.)
I think so too.

phrases.de: C'est exactement ce que je pense.
phrases.en: That's exactly what I think.

phrases.de: Je trouve que c'est une bonne idée.
phrases.en: I think that's a good idea.
OK, agreed. Ça marche is the everyday “OK, fine” among friends and colleagues.
I see it differently.
I don't agree.

phrases.de: Ce n'est pas tout à fait vrai.
phrases.en: That's not quite right.

phrases.de: Désolé, mais je ne suis pas d'accord.
phrases.en: I'm sorry, but I disagree. A polite way to say no. (A woman writes désolée; it sounds the same.)

phrases.de: Je ne crois pas que ce soit vrai.
phrases.en: I don't think that's true. (After je ne crois pas que comes the subjunctive: soit.)
I don't think so.
Yes, but … You agree a little, then add your point.
No way! (informal)

phrases.de: Je n'en suis pas si sûr.
phrases.en: I'm not so sure about that. (A woman writes sûre; it sounds the same.)
Do you really think so? (With vous: Vous croyez vraiment ?)

phrases.de: Je ne sais pas, je ne suis pas sûr.
phrases.en: I don't know, I'm not sure. (A woman writes sûre.)

phrases.de: Est-ce que c'est vraiment le cas ?
phrases.en: Is that really so?

phrases.de: J'ai du mal à le croire.
phrases.en: I find that hard to believe.
Hmm, I have my doubts.
Are you sure? (To a woman, written: Tu es sûre ? With vous: Vous êtes sûr ?)
I doubt it.
I'm so sorry. (A woman writes désolée; it sounds the same.)
Cheer up! Keep going!
It'll be all right.
Don't worry. (With vous: Ne vous inquiétez pas.)

phrases.de: Je suis là si tu as besoin de quoi que ce soit.
phrases.en: I'm here if you need anything at all.
It's not that bad. Careful: with a real problem it can sound dismissive.
You'll manage it! You can do it!

phrases.de: Je peux faire quelque chose pour toi ?
phrases.en: Is there anything I can do for you? (With vous: pour vous.)
My view is that …
I think that … The easiest way to give your opinion.
In my opinion, …
It seems to me that …
What matters to me is that … (Often followed by the subjunctive.)
To be honest, … (Franchement, … is the shorter, more relaxed version.)
That seems fine to me.
And what do you think? (With vous: Et vous, qu'en pensez-vous ?)
Sorry? You didn't hear what someone said.

phrases.de: Vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
phrases.en: Could you say that again, please? (With tu: Tu peux répéter ?)

phrases.de: Vous pouvez parler plus lentement, s'il vous plaît ?
phrases.en: Could you speak more slowly, please?
What does that mean?
Sorry, I didn't understand that.
How do you spell that?
Do you mean that …? You check that you have understood.

phrases.de: Vous pouvez me donner un exemple ?
phrases.en: Could you give me an example?

phrases.de: Vous pouvez m'aider, s'il vous plaît ?
phrases.en: Could you help me, please? A polite way to ask a stranger or an official.
Have you got a minute? (With tu: Tu as un instant ?)

phrases.de: Tu peux me passer le sel, s'il te plaît ?
phrases.en: Could you pass me the salt, please? (To someone you call vous: Vous pouvez me passer le sel, s'il vous plaît ?)
Could I ask you a favour? (With tu: Je peux te demander un service ?)
Sorry to bother you. Say this before you interrupt someone.
Could you show me?
I need some help.
Would that be possible?
Sorry! For a small mistake, or when you bump into someone.
I'm really sorry. (A woman writes désolée; it sounds the same.)

phrases.de: Je ne voulais pas dire ça.
phrases.en: I didn't mean it like that.
Sorry I'm late. (With vous: Excusez-moi d'être en retard.)
That was my fault.
No problem. An answer to an apology: it's OK.
It doesn't matter. An answer to an apology: forget it.

phrases.de: Ça peut arriver à tout le monde.
phrases.en: It could happen to anyone. An answer to an apology.
Thank you very much!
Thanks, that's very kind of you.

phrases.de: Merci mille fois pour ton aide.
phrases.en: Thank you so much for your help. (With vous: pour votre aide.)
How thoughtful of you! For a small gift or a kind gesture.
You're welcome! An answer to thank you.

frCA.note: In Québec people usually answer merci with Bienvenue! In France Bienvenue only welcomes someone arriving.

phrases.en: My pleasure. An answer to thank you.

phrases.de: Il n'y a pas de quoi.
phrases.en: Don't mention it. An answer to thank you.
I'm really grateful to you for it. (A woman writes reconnaissante. With vous: Je vous en suis vraiment reconnaissant.)
How about …? (Et si on prenait le métro ? After et si the imparfait suggests something.)
Shall we go out for a meal? (informal)

phrases.de: Je propose que nous y allions.
phrases.en: I suggest that we go. (Je propose que is followed by the subjunctive: allions.)

phrases.de: Ça te dit d'aller au cinéma ?
phrases.en: Do you fancy going to the cinema? (With vous: Ça vous dit d'aller au cinéma ?)

frCA.note: In Québec you often hear Ça te tente d'aller au cinéma ? The cinéma is the same word in both.
frCA.form: Ça te tente d'aller au cinéma ?

phrases.en: Good idea, let's do that! A yes to a suggestion.

phrases.de: Désolé, ce jour-là, je ne peux pas.
phrases.en: Sorry, I can't make it that day. A no to a suggestion.
Maybe another time.
Is Saturday good for you? (With vous: Ça vous va, samedi ?)
Congratulations! For an exam, a new job, a baby.
Happy birthday!
Good luck!
Good luck with your exam! (With vous: pour votre examen.)
Get well soon! To someone who is ill.
Have a nice weekend! Said on Friday.

frCA.note: In Québec people say Bonne fin de semaine ! (une fin de semaine). Week-end is understood but less usual.

phrases.en: Merry Christmas!

phrases.de: Je suis tellement content pour toi !
phrases.en: I'm so happy for you! (A woman writes contente. With vous: pour vous.)
Hello! Good morning. Used from morning until the evening, when you switch to Bonsoir. Always say it first when you enter a shop or an office.
Pleased to meet you. (A woman writes enchantée. Between friends or young people: Enchanté, plus tu.)
How are you? Answer: Ça va bien, merci. Et toi ? (With vous: Et vous ?)
Long time no see! (informal)
See you tomorrow!
Goodbye!
Take care! A friendly goodbye. (With vous: Prenez soin de vous !)
Have a good day! Also the usual goodbye to shop staff and officials.
In the picture I can see … The easiest way to start.

phrases.de: La photo montre une famille en train de manger.
phrases.en: The picture shows a family having a meal. You say what it is about. (en train de + infinitive = “in the middle of doing”.)
In the foreground you can see …

phrases.de: À l'arrière-plan, il y a un parc.
phrases.en: In the background there's a park.

phrases.de: Au centre, il y a une table.
phrases.en: In the middle there's a table.

phrases.de: À gauche, il y a une jeune femme assise.
phrases.en: On the left there's a young woman sitting down.

phrases.de: Dans le coin supérieur droit, il y a une fenêtre.
phrases.en: In the top right-hand corner there's a window.

phrases.de: Les gens sont probablement en vacances.
phrases.en: The people are probably on holiday. A guess about the situation.

phrases.de: Je pense que c'est une fête d'anniversaire.
phrases.en: I think it's a birthday party. A guess about the situation.

phrases.de: On dirait que tout le monde est content.
phrases.en: It looks as if everyone is happy.
The atmosphere is relaxed.

phrases.de: Cette photo me rappelle mon enfance.
phrases.en: The picture reminds me of my childhood. You connect it with your own life.

phrases.de: Le ballon est dans la boîte.
phrases.en: The ball is in the box.

phrases.de: Le ballon est sur la boîte.
phrases.en: The ball is on the box.

phrases.de: Le ballon est sous la table.
phrases.en: The ball is under the table.

phrases.de: La lampe est suspendue au-dessus de la table.
phrases.en: The lamp is hanging above the table. (Sur means “on”; “above” is au-dessus de.)

phrases.de: Le ballon est à côté de la boîte.
phrases.en: The ball is next to the box.

phrases.de: Le ballon est devant la boîte.
phrases.en: The ball is in front of the box.

phrases.de: Le ballon est derrière la boîte.
phrases.en: The ball is behind the box.

phrases.de: Le ballon est entre les boîtes.
phrases.en: The ball is between the boxes.

phrases.de: Le tableau est accroché au mur.
phrases.en: The picture is on the wall. (à + le becomes au: au mur.)
